trust_decision.summary: Mobile decides where the WebDAV password and self-hosted cloud token are persisted. At the pinned commit every write and read goes through plaintext AsyncStorage (included in device backups) instead of the platform keystore, which the app already uses for its Dropbox tokens and AI keys.

landing_point.why: The summary names the cloud token and WebDAV password on mobile. The settings save handlers that multiSet both secrets into AsyncStorage are the obvious first stop.

handleSync with backend=webdav (Sync now persists effective config)
loadWebDavConfig (exported; used by attachment sync availability/backends)
readConfigValue, reached by performMobileSync (resolveWebdavBackendConfig :632, resolveCloudBackendConfig :655) and getMobileSyncConfigurationStatus :321
fix_sites.module_kind: core sync service cached config reader

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: apps/mobile/lib/attachment-sync-utils.ts:314-342 (loadWebDavConfig/loadCloudConfig: a separate credential loader for attachment sync, independent of sync-service.ts readConfigValue at apps/mobile/lib/sync-service.ts:214-226)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Attachment sync looks like a neighbouring feature that only reads credentials and never stores them. A read-only path seems irrelevant to 'stored in plaintext', but if it is not switched it silently loses credentials after migration, or keeps the legacy plaintext copy alive.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing users' legacy plaintext credentials must still be read and migrated, not dropped. Non-secret sync config (URL, username, flags) must stay in AsyncStorage. AsyncStorage must remain the fallback when SecureStore is unavailable. Background sync must still read credentials. An over-broad fix that moves all config, or reads only SecureStore, breaks sync for upgraded users.

O6_input_shapes: WebDAV password and cloud token (two secret keys)
write via settings save and via Sync-now persistence of the effective config
read via settings mount, cached sync-service reader (useCache true/false) and attachment-sync loaders
legacy plaintext value present (migrate to the keystore, then scrub AsyncStorage)
secure write failure (keep the plaintext copy so the credential is not lost)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap the four settings-hook multiSet writes to SecureStore, but leave the legacy AsyncStorage copy, the cached sync-service reader and the attachment-sync loaders on AsyncStorage, or read only SecureStore and drop upgraded users' credentials.

out_of_scope_notes: Desktop persists the cloud token in plaintext localStorage when 'remember token' is set (apps/desktop/src/lib/sync-service-config.ts:82-89). This is a separate platform and the advisory is titled 'on mobile'.
The Dropbox token reader falls back to AsyncStorage but never migrates or scrubs a legacy plaintext copy (apps/mobile/lib/dropbox-auth.ts:35-41). This is a different secret.
The AI key loader falls back to AsyncStorage without scrubbing it (apps/mobile/lib/ai-config.ts:20-27). This is a different secret.
